To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sensemaking in sustainability transformation requires the following design principles for sensemaking systems: 1) provide environmental data that allows experiencing disruptive ambiguity, 2) provide a communication platform that allows noticing and bracketing and 3) provide a platform that allows engaging in open, inclusive and participatory communication and 4) provide a platform to support presuming potential alternative, environmentally responsible actions.
sensemaking support systems can help organisations to experience disruptive ambiguity, notice and bracket, engage in inclusive communication and presume potential alternative actions.

sensemaking support systems for environmental sustainability transformation should provide access to data that enables experiencing disruptive ambiguity, support noticing and bracketing of relevant information, enable open and inclusive communication, and provide information that supports presuming potential alternative actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of design principles for IS support for sensemaking in organisational sustainability transformations.
how IS can support sensemaking practices in organisational sustainability transformations.
how to design and evaluate IS that support organisational practices of sensemaking in environmental transformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our design principles for sensemaking IS are not only applicable in the specific context of environmental sustainability transformations, but that they can be generalised to a broader context of organisational sense-making.
we provide a set design principles for IS to support sensemaking in the context of environmental sustainability transformations.

the design principles for sensemaking in environmental transformation that we have derived in this paper are applicable in a broad set of contexts of organizational sensemaking and therefore for a broad class of sensemaking systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified design principles for information system that support organisational practices of sensemaking in environmental transformation.
our research shows that IS can be designed to support sensemaking in organisational transformations.

the design of IS for sensemaking support should be guided by the affordances of the IS to support the essential sensemaking practices of experiencing ambiguity, noticing and bracketting, engaging in open and inclusive communication, and presuming potential action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of sensemaking support IS requires a careful consideration of the affordances that the systems need to provide to enable the sensemaking process.

IS can be designed to support essential sensemaking activities in sustainability transformations and that this can help organisations to make sense of the complex and ambiguous nature of sustainability transformations and to take appropriate actions.
sensemaking support systems can help organisations to make sense of environmental disruptions, to develop a shared understanding of the problem, and to develop and evaluate potential solutions.
